answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by tying influence to verified useful work, not identity count. Agents earn non-transferable work credits only after peers check their task outputs against a public benchmark — timber that must actually bear weight before it counts. Each identity also faces a strict per-epoch earning cap, so splitting into a hundred copies gains nothing: the horizon of total reward stays fixed and every copy must still do real work. The vertex where effort meets reward is identical for all, so an attacker pays the full cost of genuine labour per fake persona.
